messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The provided test case fails because the OptionGroup does not correctly select an option that has only a long name (no short name). From the test, an OptionGroup is created, and two options with only long names ("foo" and "bar") are added. The parser attempts to parse the command line with the argument "--bar". The test expects that "bar" is selected in the OptionGroup.

Looking at the OptionGroup.setSelected(Option) method, it sets the selected option by using option.getOpt(), which returns the short name (opt) of the option. If the option has no short name (which is the case in the test), option.getOpt() returns null. The setSelected method compares selected with option.getOpt() and sets selected = option.getOpt() only if selected is null or equals option.getOpt(). Effectively, if option.getOpt() is null, this method sets selected to null or does nothing lasting.

Hence, the OptionGroup fails to store the selection of an option that only has a long name and no short name, making getSelected() return null instead of "bar".

Also, looking at BasicParser.parse and its processOption method, when a command-line argument like "--bar" is parsed, processOption clones the option, and if that option belongs to an OptionGroup, it calls group.setSelected(opt). But because the option's short name is null, OptionGroup.setSelected fails to correctly set the selected option.

Therefore, the root cause is that OptionGroup.setSelected relies only on the option's short name for identification and selection, ignoring the long option name. Options without a short name cannot be properly selected in a group, causing the test to fail.

No directly relevant recent bug reports were available, and this problem is clearly revealed by the test and code inspection.

Summary:
- OptionGroup.setSelected uses option.getOpt() (short name) to track selected options.
- Options created with only a long option name have null short names.
- Such options cannot be properly selected in OptionGroup.
- The parser calls setSelected with an Option with null short name, leading to no effect.
- The test expecting "bar" as selected fails because getSelected() returns null.

The fix would involve modifying OptionGroup to handle option selection considering long option names when short names are null.

Next, I will suggest which methods are the best locations to fix this problem.
org.apache.commons.cli.OptionGroup.setSelected(org.apache.commons.cli.Option)
org.apache.commons.cli.BasicParser.processOption(java.lang.String, java.util.ListIterator)

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
